action: Place probe on the right flank.
interpretation: Initiate scanning of the right flank region.

action: Slide the probe slightly posteriorly. Orient the probe to obtain a sagittal view.
interpretation: Visualize the right kidney in the sagittal plane.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath in.' Maintain probe position.
interpretation: Observe the kidney descend below the diaphragm. Confirm the image becomes clearer due to the displacement.

action: Sweep the probe all the way anteriorly, then sweep all the way posteriorly while maintaining sagittal orientation.
interpretation: Scan through the entire kidney parenchyma from the anterior to the posterior border.
Allow patient to relax breath hold.

action: Instruct patient: 'Roll onto your side'. Adjust probe position based on patient body habitus.
interpretation: Reposition to ensure visualization of the entire kidney, compensating for body habitus variations.

action: Maneuver the probe to use the liver as an acoustic window.
interpretation: Utilize the liver to provide a clear image of the adjacent kidney.

action: Instruct patient: 'Take a deep breath in'. Scan comprehensively from anterior to posterior in sagittal.
interpretation: Re-evaluate the kidney in the sagittal plane using the liver window and breath hold.
Convert the view of the kidney from sagittal to transverse orientation.

action: Sweep the probe superiorly to the upper pole and inferiorly down to the lower pole.
interpretation: Visualize the full extent of the kidney in transverse, ensuring coverage of both poles.
